directAnswer: To connect a motherboard, ensure all power cables, data cables, and peripheral connections are securely attached according to the motherboard manual.
summary: Connecting a motherboard involves several key steps, including power connections, data connections, and peripheral attachments. Follow the guidelines to ensure proper setup.

sections.heading: Power Connections
sections.body: Connect the 24-pin ATX power connector and the 4/8-pin CPU power connector from the power supply to the motherboard.

sections.heading: Data Connections
sections.body: Attach SATA cables from the motherboard to storage devices and connect any necessary front panel connectors (USB, audio) as per the motherboard manual.

sections.heading: Peripheral Connections
sections.body: Connect the GPU, RAM, and any additional expansion cards to their respective slots on the motherboard.

steps.title: Prepare the Case
steps.detail: Ensure the PC case is ready and the motherboard standoffs are installed correctly.

steps.title: Connect Power Supply
steps.detail: Plug in the 24-pin and CPU power connectors to the motherboard.

steps.title: Attach Data Cables
steps.detail: Connect SATA cables from the motherboard to your hard drives or SSDs.

steps.title: Install Expansion Cards
steps.detail: Insert the GPU and any other expansion cards into their slots and secure them.

faqs.question: What if my motherboard doesn't power on?
faqs.answer: Check all power connections and ensure the power supply is functioning. Also, verify that the power switch is connected to the motherboard correctly.

faqs.question: How do I connect front panel connectors?
faqs.answer: Refer to the motherboard manual for the exact pin layout for front panel connectors such as power switch, reset switch, and LED indicators.

faqs.question: Can I connect multiple GPUs to my motherboard?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your motherboard supports multiple GPUs, ensure you have adequate power and cooling for each card.

caveats: Ensure compatibility of components before connecting.
Refer to the specific motherboard manual for detailed instructions, as layouts may vary.
